result.title: A low-rank decoder bottleneck bounds reliability in foundation-model perturbation prediction
result.summary: Foundation-model predictors of perturbation response are evaluated primarily by aggregate accuracy. Using their predictions to prioritize experiments requires assessing each prediction's reliability. We audit the state-transition (ST) decoder used in STATE across three encoders (SE-600M, scGPT, and Tahoe-x1) and four cell lines under CRISPRi. The decoder's first attention layer has a low-rank output. Projecting this output onto 4-32 fixed directions estimated from training activations preserves mean per-perturbation Pearson delta correlation (PDC). This low-rank attention bottleneck bounds the decoder's reliability by distance to training responses: PDC declines as the cosine distance from a perturbation's observed response to its nearest training response increases. We propose predicted-NN-distance, the cosine distance from a predicted response to its nearest training response, as a per-prediction confidence score. The score has a mean absolute Spearman correlation of 0.81 with PDC, close to the 0.88 obtained with the observed response. Thresholds calibrated on this score transfer across encoders and cell lines, and the score remains predictive of PDC for drug perturbations.

AI.brief_summary: 论文审计 STATE 模型中 state-transition 解码器在三种编码器与四条细胞系下的行为，发现其首层注意力输出呈低秩，且预测响应对最近训练响应的余弦距离可作为逐预测置信度，与 PDC 相关性接近使用真实响应时的水平。
AI.relevance_reason: 低秩注意力瓶颈限制预测可靠性的结论，可能与 LVR 中 latent 状态信息坍缩、表示容量不足的问题相通；以「距最近训练样本的距离」作逐预测置信度，或可为判断视觉证据是否被利用及停止/弃答决策提供评价思路，可供核查其跨任务迁移性。
